marie (pm): FYI — Sales sent over a contract request from FinServCo asking for a contractual uptime of 99.99% and p95 latency <=50ms for their core inference routes. They want escalation routing and a 24/7 contact. Can we triage feasibility + what product asks we need to push?

alexa (sales): Yep — FinServCo is on a fast-track procurement timeline, asking to sign by EOM. They're willing to pay for Dedicated + support add-on but legal needs the wording. They also asked about regional failover in EU + NA.

jason (eng-infra): Quick take: 99.99% across regions is non-trivial. Options: Dedicated fleet with redundant ASGs + active-active multi-region routing + health-check failover. For p95 50ms depends on model & seq len; with smaller models + colocated infra we can aim for it. Rough effort: infra work (~2–3 sprints) + runbooks + SRE on-call burn.

dan (support): From support ops: we need a clear escalation path and SLATTLs. Proposed path: Tier1 CS -> Tier2 Support -> Eng Platform on-call -> Eng Infra pager -> Exec on-call (for business-impact). Add a dedicated response SLA: initial ack in 15m (P0), mitigation timeline 1h.

luis (legal): We need to review indemnities and force majeure + outage credit language. If we offer 99.99% we must specify measurement method (rolling 30 day vs monthly) and excluded events (customer misconfig, DDoS via customer IPs). Also want to avoid hard repo clauses without capacity commit.

ryan (cs): Suggested commercial flow: offer Dedicated + "Premium SLA" add-on (extra monthly fee) that includes 24/7 paging, quarterly runbook tests, and a 4-hour on-call response. Provide an ops health dashboard access. Customer likely accepts price if runbook/response included.

marie (pm): Proposed product ask (to create a single backlog ticket):
```
- Title: Enterprise SLA offering: 99.99% uptime + 50ms p95 for selected routes
- Scope: Dedicated customers only, must opt into multi-region & premium support
- Requirements: infra redundancy, health-check routing, SLO exporter + public dashboard, escalation playbook, legal SLA template
- Launch criteria: infra tests pass (chaos + failover), SLO measurement + billing integration, signed legal template, runbook + on-call rota
- Out of scope for Phase 1: automated cross-model fallback, per-request model-level guarantees
```
Can eng estimate and we can slot into roadmap?

jason (eng-infra): I'll spin up a rough RFC and point-estimates. Need to know: is the customer willing to commit to reserved capacity (monthly)? If yes, that lowers infra complexity a lot.

alexa (sales): They indicated yes to reserved capacity but want to keep some burst for spikes. Will confirm exact commit numbers by EOW.

dan (support): Also add a test plan for runbook validation: quarterly failover drills + tabletop exercises. Recommend a dedicated escalation Slack channel + external pager contact list.

luis (legal): I'll draft a redlineable SLA template and mark non-negotiables. Send me the measurement definitions and mitigation timelines and I'll run with it.

marie (pm): Next steps: (1) Jason to produce RFC + rough estimates by Wed (2) Luis to produce SLA draft by Thu (3) Ryan + Dan to define runbook checklist (4) Alexa to confirm reserved capacity numbers by EOW. I'll create the backlog ticket and tag priority as "enterprise-contract". @jason (eng-infra) @luis (legal) please ack.

jason (eng-infra): ack. starting RFC. :thumbsup:

luis (legal): ack, will have draft. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deployment notice — no infra changes scheduled for this thread.

marie (pm): adding note: if estimates push beyond Q2, we should propose an interim commercial mitigation (monthly SLA credits + prioritized support) so sales can keep momentum.

alexa (sales): good plan. I'll keep customer updated.

ryan (cs): I'll prepare the runbook checklist template and share in the thread when ready.

marie (pm): thanks team — will file ticket and add acceptance criteria.
